مَسْحُوتٌ (assumed tropical:) Property (مَالٌ) made to go away, or depart; made away with, made an end of, or destroyed; as also ↓ مُسْحَتٌ , (S, K,) as in a verse cited voce مُجَلَّفٌ, (S,) and ↓ سُحْتٌ and ↓ سَحِيتٌ . (K.) ―
-b2- (assumed tropical:) A man who eats and drinks vehemently; as also ↓ سَحْتٌ and ↓ سَحِيتٌ : (TA in the present art.:) and ↓ أُسْحُوتٌ signifies [the same, or] a man who eats and drinks much., (Az, TA voce أُسْحُوبٌ, q. v.) And مَسْحُوتُ الجَوْفِ (assumed tropical:) A man (S) who does not become satiated: (S, K:) having a capacious belly, (K, TA,) and who does not become satiated with food: (TA:) and as some say, hungry: (TA:) and one who suffers much from indigestion. (K, TA.) And مَسْحُوتُ المَعِدَةِ (tropical:) A man having a greedy, or gluttonous, stomach. (A, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
